newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds volatile amid scarce deals.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds volatile amid scarce deals.

text.p: Argentine bonds fell in a volatile market after the release of U.S. durable goods orders for September that were higher than expected, but then recovered in thin volume, dealers said.
"The Argentine bonds were negatively affected by the announcement the U.S. durable goods orders rose in September 4.6 percent, well above expectations," a trader for a big foreign bank said.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell to a minimum of $116.7 before recovering to 117.129 and Argentina's FRB due 2005 slipped to a minimum of 79-1/8 before recovering to 79-1/2.
"Those were the expected support levels," the trader said. "But the final stages of the year are nearing and nobody takes strong positions."

Among other factors affecting the market dealers mentioned the ongoing dispute between Argentine former Economy minister Domingo Cavallo and government officials over his charges of corruption, a decline in Brazilian bonds and a Mexican peso preopening pointing towards a fall.
